description: 1. Main processes simulated: REcoM3 simulates the coupled marine cycles of carbon, nitrogen, silicon, iron and oxygen, embedded in FESOM2 and running on the ocean mesh. The plankton ecosystem is represented at medium complexity with two phytoplankton groups, small phytoplankton and diatoms, plus a coccolithophore-like calcifying flux, two zooplankton groups, and detritus. Dissolved inorganic carbon and alkalinity are prognostic, and air-sea CO2 exchange is computed from the simulated surface carbonate system.  2. Key physics / parameterisations: Variable stoichiometry throughout, so intracellular C:N:Si:Fe:chlorophyll ratios respond to light, temperature and nutrient limitation rather than being fixed, following the regulated-quota formulation of Schartau et al. (2007) and Geider-type photoacclimation. Iron limitation and scavenging, silicon limitation of diatoms, temperature-dependent remineralisation, and sinking of detritus and calcite. Benthic layers close the budgets for carbon, nitrogen, silicon and calcite.  3. Notable features of this version: Coupled into AWI-ESM3 with prognostic atmospheric CO2, so the ocean carbon flux feeds back on the atmospheric concentration rather than being diagnosed against a prescribed one. This closes the ocean side of the carbon cycle alongside LPJ-GUESS on land.
